rule: A full-dimensional subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space equals the whole space

conditions.condition: im(T) is a subspace of V.
conditions.justification: The image of the linear map T: V -> V is a subspace of its codomain V.

conditions.condition: V is finite-dimensional and dim im(T) = dim V.
conditions.justification: Both finite dimensionality and the equality of dimensions are explicitly available.

circularity.justification: The equality im(T)=V follows from the subspace dimension lemma, and surjectivity then follows by definition.

conclusion.statement: Thus im(T) = V, so T is surjective.
conclusion.justification: A subspace of finite-dimensional V having dimension dim V must be V itself; im(T)=V is exactly surjectivity of T onto V.

reason: The conclusion is a standard finite-dimensional subspace argument followed by the definition of surjectivity.
